comments.content: - **Defect — high:** `src/Mod/Part/Gui/Command.cpp:1974` assigns the first selected curve to `curve2` instead of `curve1`. Selecting two edges—either from one object or separate objects—leaves `curve1` null, so ruled-surface creation reports “Wrong Selection” despite valid input.

- **Defect — medium:** `src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:1334` duplicates `TopAbs_SHELL` in `simplificationPriority` and omits `TopAbs_EDGE`. A compound containing exactly one edge therefore remains a compound, breaking the prior `NeedSubElement` behavior and causing edge-expecting callers to reject it or fail an edge cast.

- **Behavioral regression / future-bug risk:** `src/Mod/PartDesign/App/FeatureSketchBased.cpp:730` switches from `getTopoShape` to `getShape`, which unconditionally requests `NoElementMap`. Wrapping the resulting `TopoDS_Shape` back into `TopoShape` cannot restore its element mapping, so multi-face “up to shape” references lose stable source metadata and may stop tracking correctly after recomputation or topology changes.

- **Misleading documentation:** `src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.h:140` still documents `transform` as a boolean parameter even though the API now accepts a combined `options` bitmask. The complete option semantics, including interactions such as `DontSimplifyCompound`, should be documented here.

- **Dead code:** `src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:881` retains the removed `_getTopoShape` signature as a large commented-out fragment. It will become stale as the new interface evolves and should be removed.

## 1. `simplifyCompound` dropped `TopAbs_EDGE` and duplicates `TopAbs_SHELL` — wrong result / regression
**File: src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp** (new `simplifyCompound` at 1326–1343, priority array 1328–1335, duplicate `TopAbs_SHELL` at line 1333)

The old if/else chain simplified compounds containing exactly one `SOLID, COMPSOLID, FACE, SHELL, EDGE, WIRE, VERTEX`. The new array is `SOLID, COMPSOLID, FACE, SHELL, SHELL, WIRE, VERTEX` — `TopAbs_EDGE` is gone and `TopAbs_SHELL` appears twice (the second entry is dead code, it can never be the first `count == 1` match). Two concrete failures:

- A compound containing exactly one **edge** is no longer unwrapped; callers that type-check the result now see `TopAbs_COMPOUND`. A victim is visible in this same diff: `DlgExtrusion.cpp` (`TopoDS_Shape sub = ...getTopoShape(...); if (!sub.IsNull() && sub.ShapeType() == TopAbs_EDGE)`, line ~92 of the `@@ -82,7 +82,14 @@` hunk) — the edge-selection gate now rejects a selection it previously accepted.
- Worse, the loop returns the **first** priority class with `count == 1`. A compound containing one edge *and* one vertex previously returned the **edge** (EDGE outranked VERTEX); it now returns the **vertex**. Same input, different (wrong) sub-shape.

This fires for every `getTopoShape(..., NeedSubElement | ...)` call in this diff whose resolved shape is a compound of one edge — e.g. `FeatureExtrusion.cpp:173-178` / `FeatureRevolution.cpp:94-99` `fetchAxisLink`, `FeatureMirroring.cpp:173-179`. Almost certainly a typo, but it changes shape types returned to many callers.

## 2. Ruled Surface: `curve1` assignment became `curve2` — wrong result
**File: src/Mod/Part/Gui/Command.cpp** line 1974 (hunk `@@ -1972,11 +1971,24 @@`)

The first branch of `CmdPartRuledSurface::activated` previously assigned `curve1 = getTopoShape(docobj1, subnames1[0]...)`; it now assigns **`curve2`** (the second branch at ~1985 still assigns `curve2` from `subnames1[1]`). Consequences: for a single curve from object 1, `curve1` is never assigned; for two curves from object 1, `curve1` is never assigned *and* `curve2` is overwritten, losing the first curve entirely. In the common two-object flow, `curve2` then gets overwritten again by `subnames2[0]` (~2012), so the ruled surface is built with a null/empty first curve — broken surface or exception every time. Copy-paste regression; must be `curve1`.

## 3. `getShape` (forces `NoElementMap`) replaces `getTopoShape` before `makeElementFace` — silent element-mapping change
**File: src/Mod/PartDesign/App/FeatureSketchBased.cpp** lines 714–719 (hunk `@@ -687,7 +711,15 @@`, inside `getUpToShapeFromLinkSubList`)

Old code kept the `TopoShape` from `getTopoShape` (element map intact) and built `face = shape.makeElementFace()`. The new code calls `getShape`, which unconditionally ORs in `NoElementMap` — wiping the element map (`shape.resetElementMap()`, `Tag = 0`, hasher cleared) — and returns a bare `TopoDS_Shape`. `makeElementFace` then names the new face's elements with nothing to map back to source element names ("Face1", etc.). PartDesign "up to face" results lose stable element names, which breaks face-name references and recompute stability downstream. It's also inconsistent with the sibling branch *in the same function* (lines ~714–719 area, the empty-sub case) which kept `getTopoShape`. Note the sibling `FeatureBlendCurve.cpp:138-143` switch to `getShape` is behaviorally neutral there (the old code discarded the map via `.getShape()` immediately), so this PartDesign case is the one that actually changes behavior.

## 4. Mirroring selection gate fetches shape for `sSubName` but guards/classifies on `subString` — potential wrong element
**File: src/Mod/Part/Gui/Mirroring.cpp** line 104 (hunk `@@ -100,7 +100,14 @@`)

Old code: `getTopoShape(pObj, subString.c_str(), true)` — the fetch, the guard `if (subString.length() > 0)` (line 102) and the classification `strstr(subString.c_str(), "Face")` all used `subString`. The new code fetches with **`sSubName`**, a different variable. If the two can differ (I can't verify — the tree is empty), the shape fetched no longer corresponds to the element the gate is testing, so `isFace`/`isEdge` classification and the returned shape disagree. At minimum this is an unexplained variable switch mid-refactor; unify or confirm `sSubName == subString`. (Same file's new lines also introduce trailing whitespace after `);` — cosmetic.)

## 5. TaskSweep loop iterates `it` but always pushes `subnames[0]` — wrong result (pre-existing, but touched here)
**File: src/Mod/Part/Gui/TaskSweep.cpp** line 302 (hunk `@@ -298,7 +298,13 @@`)

`for (it = subnames.begin(); it != subnames.end(); ++it) { subShapes.push_back(...getTopoShape(docobj, subnames[0].c_str(), ...)); }` — the iterator is never dereferenced; every iteration pushes the *first* sub-shape. With more than one subname selected, the sweep is built from a duplicated first shape and the rest are ignored. This predates the PR (old line had the same `[0]`), but the refactor rewrote exactly this call and carried the bug through — while here, it should be `*it`.

## 6. Stale parameter documentation on the new signatures
**File: src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.h** lines 140–142 (hunk `@@ -130,15 +140,16 @@`)

The doc block above the new `getShape`/`getTopoShape` still documents `@param needSubElement`, `@param resolveLink`, `@param transform` — parameters that no longer exist, and the claim that `transform` is "Set to false if pmat already includes obj's transformation" is now actively misleading since the flag is a bit in `options`. Update or delete; the enum is the only correct documentation now.

## 7. Misleading parenthesization in the option expression — future-edit trap
**File: src/Mod/Part/App/AppPartPy.cpp** lines 2295–2297 (hunk `@@ -2288,9 +2288,14 @@`)

`(ResolveLink * resolveLink) | (NeedSubElement * needSub | (Transform * xform) | (NoElementMap * nomeap))` — the parentheses are unbalanced-looking and imply a grouping that operator precedence doesn't produce (`*` binds tighter than `|`, so the value is the intended flat OR). Semantically correct today, but the shape invites a misread: the `|` after `NeedSubElement * ...` visually binds the way the outer parens suggest, and any future edit (e.g. gating one term with `&&` or adding a term) can silently change behavior. Rewrite as one flag per line with `|` at line start, no extra parens.# Code Review: Part::Feature getTopoShape/getShape Refactor

## CRITICAL BUG

**PartFeature.cpp:1350 (hunk `@@ -1298,50 +1298,48 @@`)** — `simplifyCompound()` has a duplicate `TopAbs_SHELL` entry and is missing `TopAbs_EDGE` in the simplification priority array:

```cpp
std::array<TopAbs_ShapeEnum, 7> simplificationPriority = {  
    TopAbs_SOLID,
    TopAbs_COMPSOLID,
    TopAbs_FACE,
    TopAbs_SHELL,      // index 3
    TopAbs_SHELL,      // index 4 — DUPLICATE
    TopAbs_WIRE,       // index 5
    TopAbs_VERTEX      // index 6
};
```

Old code had: `SOLID, COMPSOLID, FACE, SHELL, EDGE, WIRE, VERTEX`. The new version misses `EDGE` entirely and checks `SHELL` twice. This breaks compound simplification for single-edge compounds.

**Failure scenario**: A compound containing exactly one edge (and no solids/compsolids/faces/shells) will not be simplified to that edge, returning the compound instead. This propagates incorrect topology to downstream operations.

---

## CODE QUALITY / MAINTAINABILITY

**ExportOCAF2.cpp:389 (hunk `@@ -381,7 +381,11 @@`)** — Cryptic flag composition via arithmetic multiplication:
```cpp
Part::Feature::Transform * (!sub)
```
Relies on `Transform == 4` and `!sub` being 0/1. If enum values change, this silently breaks. Use explicit bitwise composition:
```cpp
int options = 0;
if (!sub) options |= Part::Feature::Transform;
```

**AppPartPy.cpp:2295-2302 (hunk `@@ -2288,9 +2288,14 @@`)** — Same multiplication trick for all four flags with confusing parentheses:
```cpp
(Feature::ResolveLink * resolveLink) | 
(Feature::NeedSubElement * Base::asBoolean(needSubElement) | 
(Feature::Transform * Base::asBoolean(transform)) | 
(Feature::NoElementMap * Base::asBoolean(noElementMap))))
```
Error-prone and unreadable. Use explicit `if` statements or a helper lambda.

---

## DESIGN CONCERN

**PartFeature.h:55-61 (hunk `@@ -52,6 +52,16 @@`)** — Plain `enum GetShapeOptions` instead of `enum class`. Allows implicit conversion to `int` and accidental mixing with unrelated integers. No type safety for bitmask operations.

---

## MISSING DOCUMENTATION

**PartFeature.h:150 (hunk `@@ -130,15 +140,16 @@`)** — New public static method `simplifyCompound()` lacks Doxygen comment explaining its purpose, when it's called automatically, and what the `DontSimplifyCompound` flag does.

**PartFeature.h:55-61** — New `DontSimplifyCompound` flag lacks documentation on when callers should use it (e.g., FeatureHole.cpp uses it but rationale isn't clear).

---

## POTENTIAL BEHAVIORAL SUBTLETY

**PartFeature.cpp:1298 (hunk `@@ -1298,50 +1298,48 @@`)** — Compound simplification now guarded by `NeedSubElement` flag:
```cpp
if (options & NeedSubElement && !(options & DontSimplifyCompound) && shape.shapeType(true) == TopAbs_COMPOUND)
```
Old code ran whenever `needSubElement=true`. Consistent for existing callers, but the new `DontSimplifyCompound` flag (default off) changes behavior for any caller that sets `NeedSubElement` but doesn't want simplification — they must now explicitly opt out. Document this interaction.

---
